verified_facts_for_writer.clean_core_and_ai: SAP's 2026 positioning (Sapphire 2026 via ERP Today; SAP Joule pages; innobu) is that enterprise AI value depends on AI readiness, trusted data, standardized processes, and a clean core. Rationale: Business AI / Joule features assume standard processes and governed (released) APIs; a core cluttered with Z-customizations and non-standard data 'blinds' the AI and limits which AI features apply. Joule Studio (GA-era 2026) lets teams build AI agents/apps that follow clean-core principles. VERIFY exact Joule Studio availability + naming and any quoted SAP statement before printing. Frame AI-uplift numbers as reported/illustrative.
verified_facts_for_writer.integration_clean_core: Clean-core integration = API-first + event-driven. Use released OData/SOAP APIs and events via SAP Integration Suite rather than direct DB calls, RFC, or unreleased BAPI, which create hidden coupling that breaks on upgrade. SAP Integration Suite (incl. API Management with 30+ policy types) is the integration spine; the SAP Business Accelerator Hub (formerly API Business Hub) provides discoverable, versioned API contracts. SAP Event Mesh / Advanced Event Mesh for event-driven decoupling. Source: SAP Learning 'Managing Clean Core for SAP Cloud ERP'; SAP Integration Suite docs; IgniteSAP. VERIFY current product names (Business Accelerator Hub; Event Mesh vs Advanced Event Mesh).
verified_facts_for_writer.in_app_key_user_extensibility: Key-user (in-app) extensibility lets BUSINESS users (key users), not developers, adapt S/4HANA inside the system, clean-core-safe: custom fields, UI adaptation (move/hide fields on Fiori), and custom logic via the 'Custom Fields and Logic' Fiori app implementing released BAdIs. No BTP, no ABAP project. Contrast with DEVELOPER extensibility (ABAP Cloud/RAP, broader/deeper) and SIDE-BY-SIDE (on BTP). SAP note: key-user custom-field scope is broader than developer-extensibility custom-field scope; developer-extensibility custom fields only for RAP-based apps. Adaptation transport via the standard adaptation transport organizer. Source: SAP Learning key-user in-app extensibility courses; SAP Community 'Dos and Don'ts: Key User Custom Fields'. This is DISTINCT from the existing -04 (side-by-side/BTP, developer/IT audience).
verified_facts_for_writer.choosing_partner: When evaluating an SI for a clean-core S/4HANA program, ask about: custom-code inventory + Keep/Refactor/Retire approach; fit-to-standard workshop discipline (resist re-customizing); extension strategy (in-app vs ABAP Cloud vs side-by-side on BTP via released APIs); integration approach (API-first vs RFC); 'get clean, stay clean' governance + CoE; relevant certifications/tier (e.g. SAP Platinum), AMS/post-go-live model, and local/industry track record. Source: Kearney; Copado; SAP Community migration-path guidance. Soltius fit is strong and HONEST here: SAP Platinum via United VARs, Certified AMC & AMS Partner (PCoE Indonesia), Best RISE/Best Cloud awards, since 1998 / Metrodata. Keep <=3 self-mentions; partner that implements/supports, never builds.
verified_facts_for_writer.extensibility_levels_AD: Four-level model (A-D) formalized Aug 2025. A: released APIs only (ABAP Cloud on-stack or side-by-side on BTP), fully upgrade-safe, target for new dev. B: classic ABAP using only officially provided APIs/frameworks - allowed when A cannot meet the need; needs governance. C: SAP internal/unclassified objects, not cloud-ready, upgrade risk, remediation roadmap. D: explicitly non-recommended (modifications, write access to SAP tables) - eliminate. Use only as supporting context here (it is the spine of -03 maturity and the July governance pilot); do NOT make any 2026-08 article center on the A-D model.
